caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 35 of 1997.
lawyer:
Serajul Huq Senior Advocate instructed by Md Aftab Hossain Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner. 
Jamiruddin Sircar, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi. Md Wahidullah Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondents.
parties:
MA Mottalib ------ Petitioner
VS.
Narayan Kumar Agarwala and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: Petitioner, MA Mottalib. Superintendent of Customs Intelligence and Investigation Office, Tongi Circle, Dhaka filed a copy of his secret report addressed to the Director General, Customs Investigation, Dhaka to the Court of Magistrate 1st Class. Court No. 2 Nilphamari in CR Case No. 279 of 1996, which was pending between respondent No.1 Narayan Kumar Agarwala and respondent No. 2 Bijon Kumar Dev. The learned Magistrate on hearing the petitioner by order dated 29-12-96 rejected the prayer of the petitioner to seize the rice from the godown of respondent No. 1. Against the said order the petitioner filed Criminal Revision No. 5 of 1997 and the same was dismissed by the Sessions Judge, Nilphamari on 15-2-97. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the petitioner filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1083 of 1997 for quashing the proceedings of the court of Magistrate. A Division Bench of the High Court Division summarily rejected the petition on 25-2-97 after affirming the order of the learned Sessions Judge, Nilphamari. Hence this leave petition by the petitioner. 

 2. The short facts relevant for disposal of this petition are, respondent No. 1 Narayan Kumar Agarwala is an importer of rice and he under Letters of Credit dated 17-12-95 and 24-12-95 imported 100 metric tons and 400 metric tons rice respectively from India. He sold out 50 metric tons and kept the balance 450 metric tons in the go down of respondent No. 2 Bijon Kumar Dev for sale on a commission basis. Respondent No. 2 failed to sell the rice in question On 23-10-96 respondent No.1 having come to know that respondent No. 2 was trying to sell the rice surreptitiously, filed this complaint case against respondent No. 2 under sections 420/406 of the Penal Code. After the filing of the case the Magistrate 1st Class Nilphamari issued summons and in pursuance to that sale of the rice was stopped and 450 metric tons rice of Indian origin were kept in custody of Gaibandha Police. While the proceeding was continuing the petitioner as Superintendent of Customs Intelligence and Investigation submitted his enquiry report to the Court concerned stating the irregularities with regard to evasion of government revenue. The petitioners's case before the Magistrate is that a company in the name and style of Shanti Traders & Company at Natore imported 1250 Metric tons of rice from India in two consignments by two letters of credit on 10-2-96 and 19-2-96. Pending assessment of duties and other Customs formalities after arrival of the said rice in March, April, 1996 the rice was kept in the ware-house of clearing and forwarding agent of the importer namely, Messrs SM Traders. In the meantime Customs Intelligence Department got secret information that 1250 metric tons of rice imported by Shanti Traders & Company and kept in the ware-house of Messrs SM Traders have been surreptitiously removed from the said ware-house in collusion with respondent Nos. 1 and 2. The quantity of rice was removed to evade payment of customs dues. According to the petitioner 450 metric tons of rice kept in the godown of respondent No.2 was actually a part of 1250 metric tons removed from the ware-house of SM Traders without paying Customs dues. 

 4. The learned Sessions Judge found in his order that it is nobody's case that customs duty was not paid for the disputed 500 metric tons of rice imported from India. The learned Sessions Judge found that it is also very difficult after a lapse of such a long time to verify the quality of the rice as has been stated by the petitioner and further found that there is also immense scope for harassment of an innocent businessman by a custom officer on the plea of non-payment of customs duty. 

 6. The petitioner moved the Sessions Judge in revision and he having failed there has again filed an application before the High Court Division for quashing of the proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which he is precluded by law as because there was no lack of jurisdiction by the Sessions Judge to dispose of the case nor there was any erroneous exercise of jurisdiction by the court concerned. So, this is only a camouflage for filing a second revisional application. 

 8. In the facts and circumstance of the case, the Learned Judges of the High Court Division rightly refused to exercise this jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
